notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Cape Girardeau County and, in the counties that have them, the township they live in.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Missouri local candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 43 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Cape Girardeau's borders in OpenStreetMap (43 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Missouri yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 43 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Cape Girardeau's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is recorded for some; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)

redFlags.label: Gunshot detection (ShotSpotter)
redFlags.detail: In January 2022, the Cape Girardeau City Council approved a three-year, $178,200 contract with ShotSpotter.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS001912, citing Southeast MissourIan

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The City of Cape Girardeau Police Department purchased three drones in 2016.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS011228, citing KFVS 12

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Cape Girardeau Police Department has used automated license plate readers since 2013. In 2022, the agency began using Flock Safety ALPRs.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS007607, citing Columbia Daily Tribune
